Water Quality
Thermal stratification in Jocassee follows the pattern of a warm monomictic lake. Such lakes are characterized by one overturn in the fall and a winter circulation period (Ruttner, 1963). However, the data show very slight thermal gradients during the winter months (Figures 2-15 and 2-16). Minimum winter surface temperatures of about 9º10°C are reached in February. Vernal warming begins in March with thermal stratification becoming well established by late spring. Maximum temperature differences between epilimnion and hypolimnion of about 15-20°C occur in midsummer. Maximum surface water temperatures reach about 26°-27°C, while minimum hypolimnial temperatures range from about 7.5°-9.5°C throughout the year. During late summer and fall, surface temperatures begin to decline as cooling occurs. This is accompanied by a progressive deepening of the thermocline as the water becomes mixed to greater depths. It appears that the overturning of Lake Jocassee continues into the winter period, presumably because of the large volume and great depth of this reservoir.
Accompanying thermal stratification is a definite stratification of dissolved oxygen (DO). Oxygen depletion in the hypolimnion results in DO levels of less than 1.0 mg/l throughout most of the year. Depressed DO levels persist through the winter months.
Development of metalimnial oxygen maxima was observed during July at many of the lake stations (Figure 2-17). Such phenomena are often associated with the trapping of oxygen produced by photosynthesis in a high-lying metalimnion (Ruttner, 1963). Metalimnial oxygen minima are also observed in the reservoir during the late summer and early fall.
Surface DO levels tend to increase during the fall and winter months and decrease during the spring and summer months. Occasional supersaturated DO concentrations were noted in the epilimnion during the summer months.
Table 2-6 presents data for selected water quality parameters in Lake Jocassee measured at a depth of 0.3 meters. Average alkalinity values were low (4.1-4.9 mg/l) indicating poorly-buffered water. The water is also soft (average hardness of about 3 mg/l) and low in dissolved solids (specific conductances values of 11-19 micromhos/cm).
